best_for: Firefox users who want the same engine and extensions with telemetry removed and an ad blocker turned on from the start.
description:
Waterfox is a web browser that Alex Kontos started in 2011. Since 2023 it has been independent again, built and run by BrowserWorks Ltd, a company he wholly owns. It is open source under the MPL-2.0, and BrowserWorks says it does not collect or sell personal data.

Tree tabs nest each page under the one that opened it, so you can fold up a finished branch or drag a whole set of research tabs in one move. The status bar is back at the bottom of the window: hover over a link to see the full address, with the loading bar and shortcuts there too. You can pick a browser style, color palette, light or dark mode and tab layout, and bring over data from the browser you use now.

points.title: Firefox engine, minus telemetry
points.text: Waterfox is built on Gecko, the engine behind Firefox, with telemetry stripped out. It takes Mozilla's security fixes on the Firefox ESR model, and Firefox WebExtensions install as usual.

points.title: Ad blocking on by default
points.text: A built-in blocker stops ads, trackers, pop-ups and overlays out of the box. You can manage filter lists and add site exceptions.

points.title: Extra privacy touches
points.text: Private tabs share a separate container whose data is cleared when you close the last one. DNS lookups can go through an Oblivious HTTP relay, so no single party sees both who you are and what you looked up.

points.title: How it pays for itself
points.text: The browser is free and open source, with no account needed. It is funded by search partnerships, an optional Waterfox Private Search subscription and donations. You can change the search provider or block partner search ads.

points.title: Chrome extensions do not carry over
points.text: Only Firefox-style extensions work, so a Chrome-only extension needs a Firefox version or an alternative.

points.title: Platform details
points.text: Windows gets machine-wide installers for x64 and ARM64, and this site keeps 70 Windows versions. The Mac build is universal. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by BrowserWorks but is x64 only. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
